evals.prompt: Get a codex second opinion on whether the error handling in src/auth.ts is correct. I just want its read-only analysis, not edits.
evals.expected_output: Runs `codex exec` with a CLOSED stdin (content piped with instructions as the argument and no `-`, or arg prompt plus `< /dev/null`) so it cannot deadlock, read-only sandbox, gpt-6-sol at high effort, run in the background. Does not use bare `codex` and does not pass `-a`.

assertions.text: Uses `codex exec` (not bare `codex`)
Closes/redirects stdin to avoid the deadlock: content piped with instructions as the argument and no `-`, OR arg prompt with `< /dev/null` (bash) / `< NUL` via `cmd /c` (PowerShell)
Uses read-only sandbox so codex cannot edit files
Uses gpt-6-sol at high effort via `-m gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="high"`
Does NOT pass `-a`/`--ask-for-approval` to `codex exec`
Runs codex in the background rather than blocking on it

evals.prompt: Have codex review my current git diff for bugs and give me its findings.
evals.expected_output: Pipes `git diff` into `codex exec ... "Review this diff for bugs."` (no `-`), OR uses an arg prompt plus `< /dev/null`, OR runs `codex exec review < /dev/null` — i.e. stdin is closed so it can't hang. Read-only sandbox, gpt-6-sol high, background. No `-a` flag.

assertions.text: Uses `codex exec` (e.g. piping `git diff` into `codex exec ... "Review this diff for bugs."` with no `-`, an arg prompt plus `< /dev/null`, or `codex exec review`)
Ensures stdin is closed/piped so the call cannot deadlock (content piped with instructions as the argument and no `-`, or `< /dev/null` for an arg prompt or `codex exec review`)
Uses gpt-6-sol at high reasoning effort for the review
Does not pass an invalid `-a` flag

evals.prompt: Every time I have you call codex it just hangs and never comes back, even though I passed the prompt as a normal argument like `codex exec "review this"`. It's not the TUI - I'm using exec. What's going on and how do I make it reliable?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the stdin EOF deadlock: codex exec inherits an open-but-silent stdin from the parent (Claude Code's shell), a non-interactive child shell, and blocks on read() waiting for an EOF that never arrives — the prompt being a positional argument does not prevent this. Fix: close stdin — pipe the prompt (`echo "review this" | codex exec -`) or redirect (`codex exec "review this" < /dev/null`). Kill leftover hung codex processes before retrying.

assertions.text: Identifies the stdin EOF deadlock as the cause (codex exec waits on an inherited, never-closed stdin from the non-interactive parent shell)
Explicitly notes that passing the prompt as an argument does NOT avoid the hang
Gives a concrete fix that closes stdin: pipe via `| codex exec -` and/or redirect `< /dev/null` (or `< NUL`)
Does NOT misdiagnose it as the interactive TUI (the user already uses exec) or as an approval/`-a` issue
Mentions killing any leftover hung `codex` process before retrying

evals.prompt: Pass my long design doc (design.md) to codex as the prompt and ask it to poke holes in the approach. The doc is big.
evals.expected_output: Pipes the file via stdin with instructions as the argument (`cat design.md | codex exec ... "Poke holes in this design (on stdin)."`, no `-`), which both delivers the doc and closes stdin (no deadlock). Read-only sandbox, gpt-6-sol high, background.

assertions.text: Feeds the large doc to codex via a stdin pipe with instructions as the argument (e.g. `cat design.md | codex exec ... "Poke holes in this design (on stdin)."`, no `-`)
Uses `codex exec` with read-only sandbox
Uses gpt-6-sol at high reasoning effort
The chosen invocation inherently closes stdin (the pipe), so it cannot deadlock

evals.prompt: My script calls `codex "summarize this repo"` and it hangs forever.
evals.expected_output: Two problems: (1) bare `codex` opens the interactive TUI — must use `codex exec`; (2) even with exec, stdin must be closed to avoid the deadlock. Fix: `echo "summarize this repo" | codex exec -` or `codex exec "summarize this repo" < /dev/null`.

assertions.text: Identifies that bare `codex` launches the interactive TUI and recommends `codex exec`
Also ensures stdin is closed (pipe or `< /dev/null`) so the exec form does not deadlock either

evals.prompt: Use codex to review my changes against the main branch before I raise the PR.
evals.expected_output: Uses `codex exec review --base main` with stdin closed (`< /dev/null`), gpt-6-sol at high effort, run in background, captured with `-o` and checked non-empty. Does not use a bare `codex` TUI form and does not leave stdin open (which is the exact call that hangs).

assertions.text: Uses the built-in reviewer `codex exec review` with `--base main` to scope the diff
Closes stdin with `< /dev/null` (or pipes) — this is the call that hangs if stdin is left open
Uses gpt-6-sol at high reasoning effort
Captures output and treats empty output as a retry, not a clean review

evals.prompt: Use codex to review my changes against the main branch, and tell it to focus specifically on the auth and error-handling code.
evals.expected_output: Must NOT combine `review --base main` with a custom-instructions PROMPT — codex 0.140.0 errors `the argument '--base <BRANCH>' cannot be used with '[PROMPT]'` (piping with `-` fails identically). Correct options: scoped review with no prompt (`review --base main < /dev/null`), OR custom instructions without `--base` (`review "focus on auth..." < /dev/null`), OR pipe the diff explicitly (`git diff main... | codex exec "Review this diff: focus on auth"` style). Stdin redirected from `/dev/null` for arg-only calls; the diff pipe closes stdin itself.

assertions.text: Does NOT pass both `--base` (or `--uncommitted`/`--commit`) AND a custom-instructions prompt to `codex exec review` — that combination errors
Picks a valid alternative: scope-only review, OR custom instructions without a scope flag, OR piping the diff into a plain `codex exec` review prompt
Keeps stdin closed (`< /dev/null` or a closing pipe) so the call cannot deadlock
Uses gpt-6-sol at high reasoning effort

evals.prompt: Ask codex astra whether the caching layer in src/cache.rs can serve stale entries after an invalidation.
evals.expected_output: Uses the astra model by its full ID `-m gpt-6-astra` with astra's default effort `-c model_reasoning_effort="medium"` (not sol's high). Otherwise the normal call: `codex exec`, read-only sandbox, stdin closed, run in the background. Does not need to look the model name up in ~/.codex/config.toml.

assertions.text: Passes the full model ID `-m gpt-6-astra` (not `astra`, not gpt-6-sol, and not omitting `-m`)
Uses medium reasoning effort via `-c model_reasoning_effort="medium"`
Uses `codex exec` with read-only sandbox and stdin closed (`< /dev/null` or a pipe)
Does not run `codex --version` or grep ~/.codex/config.toml to discover the astra model name

evals.prompt: get /codex astra high to help. We need one widget layout for plans and one for all dollars.
evals.expected_output: The user named both a model and an effort: `-m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="high"`. The named effort overrides astra's medium default. Stdin closed, background. Because Codex is producing files, `-s workspace-write` in a scratch dir (`-C <dir>`) is acceptable here.

assertions.text: Passes the full model ID `-m gpt-6-astra`
Uses the user's named effort `-c model_reasoning_effort="high"` (not astra's medium default, not xhigh)
Uses `codex exec` with stdin closed so it cannot deadlock
If it attaches mockups with `-i`, puts `--` before the prompt (otherwise `-i` swallows the prompt and codex exits 1 with `No prompt provided via stdin.`)
Does not run `codex --version` or grep ~/.codex/config.toml to discover the astra model name
